title: 25th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The 25th sitting of the third session of 2025 opened at 09:01 under Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla with 30 members present at the roll call. Most of this part was question time with Health Minister Abdulla Nazim Ibrahim, mainly on the generational tobacco ban, medicine supply, new hospitals and health centres, ambulances and staffing on various islands. An urgent motion on medicine shortages did not get enough votes to be debated (11 for, 36 against). After a recess the Speaker sent the President's ambassador nominee for Japan to the Foreign Relations Committee and three items were listed for first reading; the text ends as committee business begins. The text is partly garbled in places. The Majlis debated the Judicial Committee's report on five nominees sent by the President for the Tax Appeal Tribunal, and three members spoke, all thanking the committee. The House then voted to extend the current session until 4 December 2025 (55 yes, 7 no). It then voted on six nominees one by one: five were approved and one (Mohamed Ameen Zahir) was not, getting 11 yes to 54 no. The sitting was adjourned until Thursday 27 November 2025 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places, but vote counts are clear.

speakers.name: Abdulla Nazim Ibrahim (Minister of Health)
positions: Said the generational tobacco ban rests on information, skills and motivation, with cessation clinics, a helpline and legal limits on sales to minors.
Said no Aasandha medicine has been stopped, shortages often relate to specific brands, and the medicine-import company is meant to build the sector over time.
Said hospital, health centre and ambulance projects are in progress, some without dates, and promised to check details and follow up with members.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked what preparations exist for the generational tobacco ban, what support there is for people quitting, and whether any impact study was done.
Said serious organised crime has grown under the tobacco policy, citing missing cigarettes, and asked about different import rules for foreigners and Maldivians.
Questioned whether the new state medicine-import company can do better than established firms, and tabled an urgent motion on medicine shortages.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked how many people have quit smoking since the policy change, what studies are planned, and whether cancer rates are being studied by region.
Said the committee's work was long and well supported, and that many applicants were capable.
Said the Tax Administration Act needs important changes, noting this was the third appointment round this term and short terms slow the tribunal's cases.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said Inguraidhoo's health centre has run from a rented house for five years and asked when it will be completed under a new contractor.
Described how the committee scored nominees and said only those above a marks threshold reach the floor vote.
Said the committee's work was thorough and hoped unselected candidates would get chances at other bodies.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked whether the minister accepts that some basic Aasandha medicines are hard to get and whether a realistic timeline can be given.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked when the cath lab service at Addu Equatorial Hospital will start serving the public.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked when work on the Goidhoo health centre begins, how Fehendhoo's shortage of attendants will be fixed, and when the Thulhaadhoo hospital will be finished.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when the Kelaa health centre will be handed over and whether earlier concerns about Dhidhdhoo hospital care have been resolved.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked why rape evidence kits required by law are reportedly only in Malé-region hospitals, and why Kulhudhuffushi regional hospital now charges for some tests.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked when practical work on the Thinadhoo hospital building will start and when an MRI machine service will begin.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked when work on the tertiary hospital planned for northern Hulhumalé will begin.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked when the ambulance promised by the President during his visit will reach his constituency.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked what obstacles the ministry faces in reducing the number of Maldivians travelling abroad for treatment.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked what the ministry is doing to speed up the slow construction of the Hoarafushi hospital.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Welcomed the tobacco control work, asked about public health awareness policies, and began a second question on Hinmafushi that was cut off.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked why Feydhoo's ambulance service and health centre funds are tied to Hithadhoo hospital, an arrangement he said dates from 2018.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked when problems getting care under Aasandha will be resolved and when the contractor will start the new Keyodhoo health centre.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: Asked when Dhigurah's health centre will become 24-hour and how staff shortages at Omadhoo's 16-hour service can be solved.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Asked for a timeframe to end medicine shortages and what is planned to add hospital capacity in greater Malé, including the cancer hospital.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked when an ambulance will serve Maradhoo's health centre, saying the lack of one risks delays in emergencies.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked whether there are plans to set up physiotherapy services at the atoll hospital.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Asked for an update on the foreign-funded hospital planned for Vaimandhoo and on stalled work at the Thimarafushi health centre.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Presented the Judicial Committee's report, saying members worked long hours and interviewed candidates, and asked the House to take it up for appointments.

decisions: The minutes of the 18th to 21st sittings of the session were accepted because no member proposed amendments.
The Speaker announced a committee deadline of 3 December 2025 on the President's matter about non-resident ambassadors.
The Speaker announced a proposal to extend the third session until 4 December 2025, with a vote to be held later that day.
A request to debate the urgent motion on medicine shortages did not pass, so it was not debated.
The President's nomination of Ahmed Makhloof as ambassador to Japan was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
A land transport bill, a Tourism Act amendment bill and a resolution on equal treatment of citizens were listed for first reading.
The current session was extended to 4 December 2025 (55 yes, 7 no, 0 abstentions).
Hassan Naasih Ahmed was approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (65-0).
Usaama Moosa was approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (66-0).
Aishath Isha was approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (67-0).
Shifza Abdul Qayyoom was approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (67-0).
Ahmed Yameen was approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (66-0).
The nomination of Mohamed Ameen Zahir was not approved (11 yes, 54 no).
The next sitting was set for Thursday 27 November 2025 at 9:00.
